label: early original-phase input of o / i / p
explanation: Mostly an input-token unit in the original phase: 90% of activation mass is at t<L, peaking at t=1-3. The strongest inputs are o (31% rate, 6x lift), i (29%) and p (18%), followed by a weaker set (2, g, u, q, 3). Even o fires on fewer than a third of its occurrences, so context matters. Activations are larger when w, s, e or t appeared earlier, and the top examples are o/i/p right after a w-rich prefix (e.g. z w w w p). Also higher on a first occurrence (in_first). Rarely fires at the delimiter and only weakly in the copy phase (10% of mass), and decays after t~5. The best simple predicate (o/i/p input at t<=4) gets dev F1 0.45 and mass recall 0.44. Widening the token set raises mass recall to 0.72 but drops precision to 0.28. Much of the remaining activity is spread across other tokens in early original positions with no clean rule.
